root_cause: The repair controller lacked a durable task-run state machine binding immutable inputs, workspace fingerprints, action attempts, blockers and evidence-complete termination. Therefore an external interruption could erase the continuation point while repeated tool calls and final rendering remained unconstrained by a persisted completion contract.
causal_chain: The fixer or Judge can produce a durable side effect immediately before the host process stops.
Without a checkpoint ledger, the next invocation cannot distinguish already-applied work from work that never ran.
Without action fingerprints and budgets, identical no-progress calls can repeat indefinitely.
Without a Completion Guard that revalidates persisted state, an unfinished or tampered task can appear complete.
rejected_hypotheses: Increasing the maximum Loop count fixes interruption recovery.
A chat summary is a sufficient checkpoint authority.
Retrying the same GitHub/log action indefinitely is safe.
A status string of COMPLETED is sufficient evidence of closure.
